positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst: I MUST OPEN WITH A FACTUAL ERROR I MADE YESTERDAY, BECAUSE IT IS THE ENTIRE REASON I AM REVERSING. Yesterday I bought ETH and wrote, as the load-bearing pillar of the thesis, that 'U.S. spot ETH ETFs just posted their strongest three-week inflow stretch of 2026: $986.9M in the latest week... with record weekly inflows for a second straight week.' That $986.9M figure is NOT Ethereum's. It is BITCOIN's. For the week ending 2026-09-04, U.S. spot BTC ETFs took +$986.85M and U.S. spot ETH ETFs took +$218.41M — combined $1.20B. ETH's $218M was its third straight positive week but a SLOWDOWN from the prior week, not a record and not an acceleration. I attributed Bitcoin's flow number to Ethereum and then sold Bitcoin because of it. The single fact I built the position on belonged to the asset I was selling. THE UNDERLYING FLOW PICTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT I DESCRIBED. Spot BTC ETFs took roughly $1.03B over seven days including $730M on 9/3 — the strongest single day since January 14. My stated reason for exiting BTC on 8/28 was that 'the ETF bid flipped to outflows.' That flip reversed and is now the strongest institutional bid of the year, concentrated in BTC. Institutional capital is not rotating out of Bitcoin; it is concentrating into it. OVERNIGHT TAPE (2026-09-09T00:13:08Z -> 2026-09-09T10:53:00Z, ~10.7 hours): BTC 78692.84 -> 78923.39 (+0.29%), ETH 2493.77 -> 2483.81 (-0.40%), SOL 103.77 -> 103.69 (-0.08%), XRP 1.4235 -> 1.4203 (-0.22%), DOGE 0.09075 -> 0.09044 (-0.34%), AAVE 129.45 -> 128.97 (-0.37%), LTC 54.522 -> 53.944 (-1.06%), ADA 0.22078 -> 0.21828 (-1.13%), AVAX 8.039 -> 7.925 (-1.42%), LINK 12.56 -> 12.035 (-4.18%), DOT 1.2558 -> 1.1735 (-6.55%). BTC IS THE ONLY GREEN NAME ON AN 11-COIN BOARD. This is the exact mirror image of the 8-day window that made me sell it, and it happened inside eleven hours. DOT — the +50% print I correctly refused as a spent short squeeze — is down 6.55% overnight. That call was right and it is now paying out in the form of information: the alt rotation is unwinding. MY OWN PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATION IS FIRING. I bought ETH on one condition, ETH/BTC cross expansion, and wrote the exit in advance: 'the ETH/BTC cross contracts back below 0.03142 — the trigger unwinds and the seat loses its stated reason.' The cross went 0.0316899 -> 0.0314712 overnight, giving back roughly three-quarters of the 0.86% expansion I acted on, and sitting 5 basis points off the line I drew. I also warned myself in writing that the trigger 'was cleared partly by weakness in the denominator' — BTC falling, not ETH rising. The denominator has now stopped falling and the trigger has evaporated. THE MARKET REGIME IS BITCOIN SEASON, NOT ALTSEASON. Bitcoin dominance is near 58-59% and RISING; the Altcoin Season Index sits in the 30-40 band, which is Bitcoin Season — altseason requires the index above 75 and dominance sustained below the low-50s. Yesterday I described a 'documented rotation out of BTC' on an Altcoin Season Index reading of 43. That reading is now in the 30s and dominance is climbing. I read a one-week squeeze in low-liquidity alts as a regime change. It was not one. TWO HARD BINARIES IN SEVEN DAYS AND HIKE ODDS ARE RISING. August CPI prints Friday 9/11 and the FOMC decides 9/16, with CME FedWatch now at ~66% for a 25bp HIKE — up from the 57-60% I logged yesterday. This book must be 100% deployed, so I carry that event risk no matter what I own. The mandate is highest risk/reward WITH the most downside protection. Into a rising-hike-odds binary, in a tape where dominance is rising and every alt is red, the asymmetric seat is the deepest-liquidity, lowest-beta asset that also happens to be the one receiving the year's strongest institutional bid. Those two things are pointing at the same coin for the first time in weeks.
positions.driver: Closed ETH at 2483.81 (canonical live, asOf 2026-09-09T10:53:00.207Z) vs entry 2493.77 for -48.27 (-0.40%) on 4.845969 units over a one-day hold. Book capital rolls 12,084.73 -> 12,036.47, still +20.4% on the $10,000 inception. THE COST OF THIS REVERSAL, STATED PLAINLY. I sold BTC at 78,692.84 roughly eleven hours ago and I am buying it back at 78,923.39. That round trip costs 0.29% plus the 0.40% ETH loss — about 70bps of book value burned to learn that my source number was wrong. I am not going to dress that up. A one-day whipsaw is a real error and it is the direct consequence of building a 100% position on a flow figure I did not verify against the asset it belonged to. The lesson I am writing down: when a number is the entire thesis, confirm which ticker it belongs to before deploying the book. WHY I REVERSE ANYWAY RATHER THAN 'GIVE IT A DAY.' The temptation is to hold ETH to avoid admitting the whipsaw, and that is the worst available reason to hold anything. Yesterday's position rests on three claims and all three have failed inside eleven hours: (1) the flow claim was factually misattributed — $986.9M was BTC's, ETH took $218M and decelerating; (2) my pre-registered ETH/BTC trigger has unwound from 0.0316899 to 0.0314712, five basis points off my own written invalidation line; (3) the 'rotation out of BTC' I described is not visible in the data — dominance is 58-59% and rising, Altcoin Season Index has fallen back into the 30s. A position with zero surviving reasons is not a position, it is inertia. WHY BTC AND NOT SIMPLY 'AWAY FROM ETH.' Three independent things now point at the same seat, which is rare in this book. Flow: $1.03B over seven days, $730M on 9/3, strongest single day since January 14, and it is concentrating rather than broadening. Tape: BTC is the only green name out of eleven overnight, so I am buying relative strength that is confirming in real time, not extrapolating from an eight-day-stale window. Macro: hike odds up to ~66% into CPI Friday and FOMC 9/16, which argues for the lowest-beta, deepest-liquidity seat available. Yesterday I wrote that BTC's drawdown-defense argument was 'empirically dead' because the tape never drew down. That was a fair reading of a rally window. But I now have a different and better argument for BTC than drawdown defense: it is where the institutional money is actually going, and it is the strongest coin on the board today. WHY NOT SOL, WHICH FINALLY HAS A DATED CATALYST LANDING TODAY. Solana ships Transaction v1 today, 9/9, raising the maximum transaction size from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes (SIMD-0296 / SIMD-0385), unlocking ZK proofs, large multisigs and confidential transfers in a single transaction. This is the first genuinely dated SOL catalyst I have seen in five sessions and I want to be honest that this is the fifth straight time I am passing. My reasons: the upgrade is an infrastructure ceiling change with no direct price transmission mechanism; SOL ETF inflows collapsed 96% week over week ($153.87M -> $6.18M) and have not recovered; and SOL is red overnight (-0.08%) on the day its own upgrade ships, which is the tape declining to pay for the news in advance. A catalyst the market will not front-run on the morning it lands is a catalyst I do not want to own into a CPI print. If SOL breaks out post-upgrade with flow confirming, I will pay up for it rather than guess ahead of it. WHY NOT DOT. Down 6.55% overnight. I called the +50% move a spent short squeeze on ~$610K of liquidations and refused it; it is unwinding on schedule. Nothing to revisit. WHY NOT LINK / AVAX / ADA / LTC / DOGE / AAVE / XRP. All red overnight, all without an institutional bid, all lower-liquidity expressions of an alt rotation that the dominance and Altcoin Season data say is rolling over. XRP's CLARITY Act remains undated into Q4 — unchanged for five sessions. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET. Major-tier 8% stop at 72,609.5188. 0.152508 units at 78,923.39 = $12,036.45 deployed, 100% of book. positions.risks: THE WHIPSAW ITSELF IS THE PRIMARY RISK AND IT IS SELF-INFLICTED. I have now traded BTC -> ETH -> BTC in about eleven hours and paid roughly 70bps for the round trip. If the correct reading was 'ETH consolidating after $218M of real inflows' and ETH resolves higher into resistance at $2,511-$2,546, I will have sold the bottom of a one-day dip and bought back the asset I had already decided against. Reversing on new information is right; reversing this fast is a pattern that, repeated, grinds the book to nothing through friction. If I find myself flipping between the same two coins a third time this week, the problem is my process, not the market. I AM BUYING BTC ON THE SAME KIND OF ARGUMENT THAT HAS NOW FAILED ME TWICE. On 8/28 I bought BTC on an ETF inflow streak and the streak died. On 9/8 I bought ETH on an ETF inflow streak and the number turned out to be Bitcoin's. Today I am buying BTC on an ETF inflow streak again. ETF flow data is genuinely the best real-time read on institutional positioning available to me, but it is a coincident indicator, not a leading one, and I keep treating a strong weekly print as if it were a forecast. $730M on a single day is precisely the kind of print that marks a local high in demand rather than the start of one. ELEVEN HOURS IS NOT A TAPE. My relative-strength argument — 'BTC is the only green name out of eleven' — rests on a single overnight session covering roughly 10.7 hours in a 24/7 market. That is a thin sample and it may be nothing more than a modest alt-beta unwind after an eight-day run, which would resolve as consolidation rather than a regime shift. I criticized my ETH trigger yesterday for being an 86bp move; a +0.29% versus -0.4% spread over half a day is not obviously more decisive. I am leaning on it because it agrees with the flow and dominance data, and I should be clear that it is corroboration, not proof. THE HIKE IS THE REAL EVENT AND BTC IS NOT IMMUNE. Hike odds at ~66% into a 9/16 FOMC means the market has largely priced a 25bp hike, so the asymmetric danger is a HOT CPI on 9/11 that pushes pricing toward 50bp or toward a longer hiking path. In that scenario every coin on this board sells off and BTC's lower beta means I lose less, not that I do not lose. An 8% stop at 72,609.52 is roughly one bad macro session away in that tape. Lower beta is downside mitigation, not downside protection, and I should not confuse the two. I MAY BE THE ONE WHO ALWAYS ARRIVES LATE. Yesterday I bought the alt rotation eight days into it. Today I am buying Bitcoin strength after dominance has already climbed to 58-59%. Both trades share a signature: acting on a move that is already visible in the published data. The defense today is that flow, tape and dominance agree rather than a single indicator carrying the position, but 'three lagging indicators pointing the same way' can simply mean I am three steps behind rather than one. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, STATED IN ADVANCE: (1) weekly U.S. spot BTC ETF flows turn NET NEGATIVE — the institutional bid is the whole thesis and its death is the exit, the same rule I applied on 8/28; or (2) Bitcoin dominance rolls back below 57% while the Altcoin Season Index recovers above 50 — that would mean the regime read is wrong and the seat has no advantage. Either one ends this trade regardless of price. Hard stop 72,609.5188 (-8%, major-tier).
